assertions: Sir William Waller overcomes in the engagement of Friday 29 March 1644 near Alresford / Cheriton, Hampshire — Waller's side wins the day
Sir Ralph Hopton is defeated and forced to give ground / retreat, his army unable to hold the field against Waller
Hopton receives no ready supplies or effective assistance: only Mars and the South Node in the 9th, his significator Saturn unaspected and isolated

Waller's substance and assistants are strong and effective: the Sun, lord of his substance/assistants, is in the 10th in the exact degree of his exaltation at 19° Aries, giving him resources, support and honour/victory

Waller's own significators are fortified — Ascendant and Moon, with Jupiter and Venus for his side, and the Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light — so his force gains strength as the fight proceeds

Hopton's significator Saturn is sub radiis, in his fall, peregrine and in no aspect to any planet, squaring the cusp of his own 7th house — his power is eclipsed, debilitated and self-afflicted, not merely outnumbered
method: Horary astrology in Lilly's classical method — comparison of essential/accidental dignity and condition of the 1st-house significators (for Waller) versus the 7th-house lord Saturn (for Hopton)
reasoning: Waller side: Moon exalted and with Jupiter (great benefic), Jupiter and Venus assigned to Waller, Sun lord of Waller's 2nd/substance in angular 10th at exact exaltation degree 19° Aries, Moon swift and increasing in light 11° from Venus. Hopton side: 7th lord Saturn in fall, peregrine, sub radiis, unaspected by any planet, square its own house cusp, with no supplies shown (Mars and South Node alone in the 9th). Strong, angular, exalted and assisted significators overcome a fallen, combust/under-beams, peregrine and isolated significator — the querent/1st-house party prevails decisively on the day.
summary: Waller should overcome Hopton at Cheriton on 29 March 1644; Hopton, unsupported and debilitated, is beaten and retreats.
